title: Withdrawal and Fall of Saigon Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace My Lai, the anti-war movement and the fall of Saigon.
meta_desc: GCSE History — My Lai, Vietnamization, Paris Accords and 1975.
final_note: You learned how the US left in 1973 and Saigon fell in April 1975.

Nixon's plan to hand fighting to ARVN troops
1970 secret raids on Khmer Rouge bases

walkthroughs.body_html:
On 16 March 1968 Lt William Calley's platoon massacred about 500 civilians at My Lai.

The cover-up unravelled in 1969. Combined with the draft and bombing, the anti-war movement exploded — 500,000 marched in Washington in November 1969. Kent State National Guards shot 4 students dead in May 1970.

Nixon, elected 1968, promised peace with honour.

Vietnamization handed combat back to the South Vietnamese army. But Nixon also secretly bombed Cambodia from 1970, and Kissinger negotiated with Le Duc Tho in Paris.

The Paris Peace Accords (27 January 1973) brought a ceasefire and US withdrawal.

Congress cut aid to Saigon. North Vietnamese tanks rolled into the city on 30 April 1975 — the Fall of Saigon. About 58,000 US troops and 2-3 million Vietnamese had died.
